name: Musaed al-Jarrah

summary.text: Musaed al-Jarrah was a Saudi diplomat at the Saudi embassy in Washington, D.C., where he led Islamic affairs, and one of the three main subjects of the FBI's Operation Encore investigation into possible Saudi government support for the September 11 hijackers. His name became public in May 2020 when it was included in an FBI court declaration by mistake. FBI records released under Executive Order 14040 describe him as an influence on Sunni extremist activity in Southern California, while a 2021 FBI memo said there was no evidence he had direct contact with the two hijackers; the casefile's closing material states that the evidence did not establish that he, Fahad al-Thumairy and Omar al-Bayoumi knowingly conspired to assist the hijackers. He has not been charged.

facts.claim: FBI records released in November 2021 under Executive Order 14040 described al-Jarrah, a Saudi embassy official in Washington, as a controlling, guiding and directing influence on Sunni extremist activity in Southern California; a September 2021 FBI memo in the same release said there was no evidence that he had direct contact with the two hijackers. These are FBI assessments, not findings of fact.
